en.name: WiFiTrail
en.short_description: Mobile app Wi-Fi security auditor and credential trial utility

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing WiFiTrail.

Please read this before you open it, because it explains what would otherwise look broken.

WiFiTrail does not scan for Wi-Fi networks, does not read the network the device is on, and does not measure throughput. iOS gives apps no API to enumerate nearby networks, and this build contains no networking code at all. The five networks in the list, the connection details (ISP, IP, DNS, gateway, MAC), the security checklist and the A+ score are fixed sample content declared in lib/domain/models.dart. The speed test is a five-second animation that always ramps to the same figures - 947 Mbps down, 473 up, 12 ms ping, computed from a step counter in lib/domain/speed_test.dart - so it will read identically on Wi-Fi, on cellular and in airplane mode. Only the Analyzer tab's channel-utilisation bars vary, and those are randomised on each scan.

In its present state this is a demonstration of those four screens, not a working Wi-Fi auditor, and we would rather you heard that from us than concluded the scanner had failed on your device.

No account, no sign-in, no demo credentials, no in-app purchase, no network access and no permission prompts of any kind.

Test instructions:
1. Launch onto the Scanner tab: a connected-network card and a list of five networks with signal, band, channel and security. Tap "Scan" - a three-second progress animation runs, after which the same fixed list is shown and the analyzer bars are re-rolled.
2. Analyzer tab: utilisation bars for channels 1, 6, 11, 36 and 149.
3. Speed Test tab: tap "Start Speed Test" and watch the ramp described above.
4. Security tab: the fixed A+ score and the five checklist rows.
5. The interface follows the device language and is translated into the twelve languages the app ships (English, Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian and Chinese). The globe button in the header opens a picker to override it. Two captions on the Speed Test tab are still English in every locale.

Privacy:
• Data collected: nothing. There is no account, no sign-up and no profile, and nothing is written to the device except the language you pick.
• Network: none. The app has no HTTP client and makes no requests.
• Tracking: none. There is no advertising or analytics SDK; the advertising identifier is not read and no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears. A Firebase Crashlytics bootstrap is present but inactive - no Firebase configuration file is included.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.

_blocked.no_copy_drafted: No listing copy can be written. It neither scans Wi-Fi nor measures speed.
_blocked.evidence: lib/domain/models.dart: 'The network list, security checklist and connection details were static in the original app and stay static here' — networks is a const list ('HomeNetwork_5G', 'Office_WiFi'). lib/domain/speed_test.dart computes readings from a step counter (download = step * 94.7) over 25 x 200ms ticks and transfers no bytes; the idle display is a hard-coded 947/473/12. pubspec has no wifi, network-info, or connectivity plugin.
_blocked.to_unblock: Implement real scanning and a real throughput test, or withdraw. A speed test that reports 947 Mbps in airplane mode will be caught in review.
